just fyi I've been digging into this and can reproduce the slowdowns, working on isolating it to something more specific (removing the included `next` component library etc).

So I managed to make much smaller test case to reproduce this, with some notes . link - https://codesandbox.io/s/ppjm15v9pq WARNING - `depth=7`/`isLazy=true` WILL LOCK YOUR BROWSER. have a look at the code and comments (and possibly run it) to see the behaviour. Anyway. When `isLazy=false`, the tree should render just fine. I was able to render `depth=13` without _much_ trouble. But when `isLazy=true`, it renders fine till `depth=5`. when `depth=6`, it hits a some kind of cliff and locks the CPU/GPU up for MANY seconds. with `depth=7`, chrome has to be force closed. We fire a SHIT TON of `retrySuspendedRoot` calls after the initial burst of js eval. Even though the calls take <0.5μs, react appears to yield back to the thread for 10μs, and then call it again. At this point, I've reached the limit of my understanding of the codebase. I'll dive in some more over the weekend and see if I can figure more out.
